the effects of umbilical blood mononuclear cell (UCBMC) transplantation via lateral ventricular injection on the neural apoptosis, the expression of Bcl-2 and Bax proteins in neonatal rat with hypoxic-ischema brain damage.

the use of cord blood stem cells for the treatment of hypoxia ischemic brain damage in neonates is a promising therapy, but more research is needed.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the umbilical cord mononuclear cells (UCMCs) transplantation via lateral ventricular (LV) can improve the neural apoptosis and decrease the Bax and Bax/Bcl-2 ratio in rats with hypoxic ischemic brain injury (HIBI), and the mechanism may be that UCMCs transplantation could increase the expression of Bcl-2.

umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (UCMSCs) transplantation can protect against brain injury and promote brain repair after hypoxia-ischemic brain injury (HIBI) in neonatal rats by inhibiting the neural apoptosis and up-regulating the ratio of Bcl-2/Bax protein expression.

the umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells transplantation could improve the neurological function and the brain structure, and reduce the neural apoptosis of the neonatal rat with hypoxic-ischaemic brain damage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of umbilical blood cells in the treatment of neonatal brain damage is a promising treatment.
the umbilical cord mesenchymal stromal cells are able to differentiate into neurons in vitro and in vivo.

we have shown that a single injection of UCB-MNCs into the lateral ventricle of the neonatal brain is sufficient to reduce the severity of hypoxic-ischemia-induced brain damage and that this effect is mediated by the activation of Bcl-2 and Bax proteins.
